compatibilityRisks: API: new routes POST /api/urls/{code}/extend and PUT /api/urls/{code}/expiry. The analytics/stats JSON gains an additive remainingSeconds field, and all existing fields are unchanged.

Code: IUrlRepository gains TryReplace, so any other test double implementing the interface will no longer compile. ShortenerService gets an optional trailing logger parameter and LinkStats an optional trailing field, so existing constructor calls still compile.
Behaviour: a missing or wrong owner returns 403, because deactivate has no 401 case. The check order is 404, 403, 400, 409. An invalid body from a non-owner therefore gets 403 first.

Rate limit: extend shares the create limiter's limit (30 per 60 seconds) under a separate 'extend:' key per client. A burst of more than 30 concurrent extends from one client gets 429, which could conflict with a 50-concurrency load test.
Security: the owner identity is the spoofable X-Client-Id header, so the audit actor hash is unverified. Audit logs go to the ILogger sink only and are not durable.
Performance: the CAS retry loop is bounded at 10,000 attempts and then throws, which returns 500 through the exception handler. This is unlikely at 50 concurrent requests.
Behaviour: a non-integer additionalSeconds such as 1.5 returns 400. An additionalSeconds above the cap of MaxExpiryMinutes*60 returns 400 (TooLong).
alreadySatisfied: FR-4: redirect, create and deactivate code paths are untouched, and GET /api/urls/{code} already returns the stored ExpiresAt, so it reflects the extension.
The 365-day cap reuses the existing MaxExpiryMinutes option (60*24*365).
note: Proposed by the developer agent. NOT applied to the repository; validated in a sandbox and exported for human review.
